description: Feature normalization: each of three features is centred by its mean and scaled by its spread, every position on its own.

line_docs: Array reading: subtract the means from the features, divide by the spreads, all positions at once; the lengths must agree at run time.
Tuple reading: the same four names declared as fixed 3-tuples, so arity and the shared index space are known before running; the expression above is unchanged.
m.purpose: Line one: the array reading, every entry at once, no index. Line two: the tuple-typed reading, declaring X, Μ, Σ and Z as fixed 3-tuples. The expression does not change; what changes is what the language knows before running: arity three, one shared index space, a result of arity three, and no length mismatch possible at run time. Placeholder glyphs.
m.text:
Z ← (X − Μ) ÷ Σ
X Μ Σ Z : Tuple[3]
m.title: The same computation, with and without homogeneous tuples

line_docs: The rule at position i: subtract the mean of feature i from feature i, divide by its spread.
The index space: i is one of the three positions, and the rule holds at each of them independently.
math.purpose: Line one is the scalar rule for one feature i. Line two says where i lives: the finite index set Fin(3), the three positions. The whole computation is that one rule applied at every position independently; no position needs another, so there is no sum.
math.title: The rule at one position, and the index space

name: feature-normalization

docs: The output: three numbers, each feature expressed in units of its own spread, zero at its mean.
Which feature: 0, 1 or 2. The stone's time axis steps through the positions.
Definition: the left side is computed from the right side.
Open parenthesis: group the difference before dividing.
The input: three raw feature values, here the RGB channels of a pixel, 120, 80 and 200.
Centre: take the feature's mean away, so zero means average.
The mean of each feature over the data it was measured on: the ImageNet channel means 123, 117, 104.
Scale: divide by the feature's spread, so one means one standard deviation. In the notation, ÷.
The standard deviation of each feature: 58, 57, 57.
i ranges over the index set: it takes each of its values.

Fin(n) is the set of positions 0 to n−1. A fixed 3-tuple of numbers is the same thing as a function from Fin(3) to numbers: that is the Naperian (representable) view the tuple line on the M face makes explicit.
How many features there are; the arity of every tuple here.
Declares the type of what is on its left.

Tuple[3]: exactly three numbers, structurally, not a list that happens to have three. With it the language knows the arity and the shared index space before running; without it the same expression runs on arrays and checks the lengths at run time.
Open bracket of the tuple's arity.

title: Feature normalization

visual.purpose: One lane per position: x and μ into −, then ÷ σ, into z; the lane being computed is lit. The right panel is the applicative view: each index maps to its triple, the same rule f is applied, and a z comes out; the lanes never touch.
visual.title: Three independent lanes, and the index space they share
